question: Should agent tools be allowed to inspect only their own dispatch capacity, or a redacted cross-agent queue/workload snapshot for scheduling decisions?
rationale: The technical queue state is internal, but the appropriate visibility scope and the relationship between agent dispatch data and operator diagnostics are product and authorization decisions that implementation should not guess.

options.title: Scoped agent dispatch view
options.body: Expose only the invoking agent’s usable spawn capacity and lane pressure, keeping other agents’ session and task metadata private.

options.title: Redacted global scheduler view
options.body: Expose aggregate cross-agent capacity and queue counts while withholding session identifiers, task content, and owner-specific details.

options.title: Operator-only diagnostics
options.body: Keep queue snapshots on CLI/RPC diagnostics and defer agent-facing scheduling until an authorization model is approved.

recommendation.title: Scoped agent dispatch view
recommendation.body: Expose only the invoking agent’s usable spawn capacity and lane pressure, keeping other agents’ session and task metadata private.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest available history links this person to both the queue/gateway implementation and agent-tool surface affected by the decision.
